The manipulation of time in the story is very effective and well-balanced, serving to build suspense and atmosphere. The narrative begins with a brief **compression of time**, summarizing the months between June (when the neighbor returned the key) and the present November afternoon in the first two paragraphs. Once the narrator enters the house, the story shifts to **stretching of time**, slowing down to match real-time or even slower. A simple, brief action—lifting the lid of a coffee tin and smelling the beans—is stretched across two paragraphs through sensory details, memories of Sunday mornings, and the shocking realization that the twenty-year-old empty tin now holds fresh beans. This deceleration creates a quiet, eerie tension that makes the sudden, abrupt final sentence ("A door slammed in the courtyard. I didn't move.") hit with maximum dramatic impact.
